segmenti.tekst: نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين.

قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون. Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Dear brothers, respected members of the congregation, suppose that today, in today's hutba (Friday sermon), I told you the story of a man whose mother carries him in her womb for nine months, and then gives birth to him, and then his parents raise him in the best possible way, giving him the very best they have,

in upbringing, in material things, and so on. And after this man grows up, reaches adulthood, strength and maturity, he leaves his parents for no reason, not wanting to be obedient or dutiful to them.
What would you think of such a man? What would you think of such a man? I am sure your opinion would be very negative. That your opinion of this man would be very negative.

Imagine, dear brothers, there is a man worse than this one, a far worse man, an incomparably worse person, and that is the person, dear brothers, to whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has given those same parents, to whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has given provision, given him a wife, children and wealth.
The blessing of hearing, of sight, just the blessing of sight alone. Dear brothers, I am sure that none of us would think for a single second of selling his blessing of sight for a billion euros.
And imagine, such a man, to whom Allah has given everything, is disobedient to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. As I said, this second person is incomparably worse than the first.

And you will see that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, calls His servants: "Wa aqimus-salah" (establish the prayer), and he is not at the dawn prayer, Fajr. And not only is he absent from Fajr in the mosque – he does not pray it even at home. Yet he has set his alarm clock to wake up for work at seven o'clock, so that he would not be late, so that his boss would not reprimand him. He is not there at Dhuhr, he is not there at Asr, even though Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, commands us to worship Him, as He says: "bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal" – in the morning and in the evening. He is not there to give zakat.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, calls him to be good to his parents, to show kindness to his parents: "And show kindness to parents." He is not there either. To show kindness to the near neighbour and the distant one, as He commands us: "Show kindness to the near neighbour and the distant neighbour." We are not there either. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says:

"وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا" – and when you speak, speak well, justly, do not utter lies. All of this, dear brothers, is Islam… And a fair measure, and that scale – do not cheat on the scale, on the measure. All of this, dear brothers, is Islam… But some people are disobedient to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, even though He has given them everything, even though He has commanded them all of this, and Allah commands nothing except what is beautiful and good for the believer.

And despite that, there are people who are disobedient to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And then, when some evil befalls him, when some evil befalls him, he blames Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, he blames someone else.

He himself is to blame. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Man 'amila salihan fa li nafsihi" – whoever does good deeds does them for himself, he does good deeds for his own sake – "wa man asa'a fa 'alayha" – and if he does evil deeds, he does evil to himself, he acts against himself – "wa ma Rabbuka bi zallamin lil-'abid" – and your Lord, your Lord who created you, will not wrong His servants; rather, the servants wrong

themselves through their disobedience. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Kullu ummati yadkhulunal-Jannata illa man aba." He says: all of my ummah will enter Jannah (Paradise), except, except, except the one who refuses. So the companions asked him: "Are there really people who will refuse to enter Jannah,
O Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Whoever follows me will enter Jannah. And whoever does not follow me will not enter Jannah."

Clear mathematics, logic, call it what you will. So, whoever follows the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and is obedient to him… And whoever obeys Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, obeys Allah, as the Qur'an says: "Man yuti'ir-Rasula faqad ata'allah." Whoever obeys Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, obeys Allah. Why? Because the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is Allah's Messenger on this Earth, entrusted with conveying to us the revelation
from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And he commands us, and he commands us nothing except what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, commands us through him.

Therefore, that is how it is, brothers: when something bad befalls us, it is from ourselves. And when something good comes to us, it is from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And a person must not be disobedient to the One who has given him, given him everything.
I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us, make us His obedient servants. I ask Him, the Exalted, to admit us into Jannah. Amin.

Ya Rabbal-'alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'anil-'azim, wa nafa'ani wa iyyakum bima fihi minal-ayati wadh-dhikril-hakim. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwal-Ghafurur-Rahim.
